title: Breadboard Connectivity Explorer
creator: Dan McCreary
subject: Clocks and Watches with AI
description: Hover over any hole of a half-size breadboard to light up every hole it is connected to, add jumper wires, peek at the hidden metal strips with X-ray view, and test yourself in Challenge mode.

educational.topic: How the holes of a solderless breadboard are connected
learningObjectives: Analyze which holes on a breadboard are electrically connected.
Explain why the center channel and the separate + and − rails matter.
Predict how a jumper wire changes which holes are connected.
prerequisites: Read the Breadboard section of Chapter 2.

accessibility.notes: Screen-reader description provided; all controls are standard HTML elements.

controls.label: Breadboard holes
controls.description: Highlights every hole connected to the hole under the pointer.

controls.label: Breadboard holes
controls.description: Two clicks add a jumper wire between two holes.

controls.label: Challenge / Free play
controls.description: Switches between free exploration and the yes/no connection quiz.

controls.label: Yes / No / Next question
controls.description: Answer the current Challenge question and move to the next one.

keyQuestions: Are holes c12 and h12 connected? Why or why not?
Why do strips run along columns and not along rows?
How many holes are connected to one hole on a power rail?
commonMisconceptions: Thinking holes in the same lettered row are connected across the board.
Thinking a column strip runs across the center channel.
Thinking the + and − rails are connected to each other.
assessmentOpportunities: Students score at least 8 out of 10 in Challenge mode.
Students can state which holes are connected to any given hole without the MicroSim.
Students explain why connecting the + rail directly to the − rail is dangerous.
